Heavy Rains Trigger Landslides, Disrupting Tourism Sites in Northern Vietnam

Heavy rainfall over the past week has led to a series of landslides affecting popular tourism sites in the northern mountainous region of Vietnam, causing significant damage to industry-owned premises and disrupting operations across several key destinations.

According to the Vietnam Tourism Operators Association, at least six major tourism sites in Lao Cai and Ha Giang provinces have reported landslides since Tuesday. Among the affected locations are scenic viewpoints, trekking trails, and cultural heritage parks managed by tourism enterprises. The Sa Pa Highlands Eco-Tourism Zone, operated by Green Valley Adventures, has seen extensive soil movement that has damaged visitor walkways, viewing platforms, and reception facilities.

“We are facing unprecedented challenges,” said Nguyen Thi Lan, site manager at Green Valley Adventures. “Several of our nature trails are now buried under meters of mud and debris, making them inaccessible and unsafe for visitors and staff.”

Tourism companies have evacuated hundreds of workers from vulnerable facilities and temporarily suspended guided tours and outdoor activities at affected sites. Locally-based tour guide Pham Van Duy described the current situation as “the most severe disruption to tourism work in recent years,” noting that staff have been redirected to assist with damage assessment and emergency response.

Industry leaders estimate that more than 220 hectares of tourism-managed land have been impacted, with losses to on-site infrastructure, equipment, and planted landscapes still being assessed. “We are working around the clock to monitor landslide risks and safeguard our employees,” said Hoang Minh Tam, spokesperson for VietHeritage Tours, which operates historical and eco-tourism premises in the region.

The Vietnam Tourism Operators Association has called for industry-wide coordination to support affected workers and sites. “Our immediate priority is the safety of staff and guests, and we urge all tourism firms to maintain strict safety measures as rainfall continues,” the Association stated in a public notice.

With further heavy rain forecast, tourism operators are bracing for ongoing disruption in the coming days.
